question: Why did prompts on 0.2.7 run at 42-46 t/s (and 415-750 t/s for long ones) while other conversations answered, freezing them for 19-79 s, and is running a prompt in a pass of its own faster?
machine: GTR9 Pro, Ryzen AI Max+ 395, 96 GB GPU carve, Windows 11, TheRock ROCm 10.2.0a20260925
model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-IQ4_XS, f16 K/V, sparse attention on
tool: tmp/ragged/multi_deep_probe.py --evict --restore (4 slots, kv_pool 512000, MTP off, disk tier on): E ~60K answered and left idle; A 88K, B 49K, C 74K streamed, each starting once the previous one streams; D a new 2.4K-token chat taking E's slot; E again with a 3.9K-token tail read back from the disk tier; F a new 837-token chat

root_cause.kernel_limit: qsa3 (ggml_cuda_flash_attn_ext_qsa_supported) declined k->ne[1] > 262140: its union list held 16-bit block numbers (65535 blocks of 4 cells)
root_cause.fallback: the generic flash-attention kernels ignore the selected indices (src[5]); the prompt-sized graph was maskless (n_tps >= 128), so every query attended densely to every cell of the window

root_cause.node_timing_E_tail_ubatch: 40.0 s: 12 x FLASH_ATTN_EXT [256,24,2051] 36.6 s; index scoring and visibility over 68480 blocks ~1.2 s
root_cause.half_size_run: 136K cells in all: under the limit, no stall (E tail 709 t/s)

columns: others' longest pause during E tail s
